name: Creaky Floorboards
tagline: Two retired ladies. One microphone. Zero correct answers (until week four).
notes: Plays automatically on the radio at the start of each day (week 1-4) while the player explores; nobody can be talked to until it ends. ep5 plays after the final inspection if the house passed. Lines are 'Speaker: text'; *...* lines are sound cues. Each episode is ~30 seconds.

ep1.title: Episode 1: The Catfish of Heartbreak Lane
lines: *Theme music: a creaky door, then a kazoo.*
Bev: Welcome back to Creaky Floorboards! I'm Bev.
Trish: And I'm Trish. We solve the mysteries the police were too busy to care about.
Bev: This week: 12 Heartbreak Lane. Condemned. Damp. And some young flipper's just bought it.
Trish: Neighbors report dripping. At night. Inside the walls.
Bev: My theory? A catfish. Enormous. Lives in the walls, eats the drywall, comes out at night.
Trish: Bev, I think SHE'S being catfished. Who's texting her at two in the morning?
Bev: THE CATFISH, Trish.
Trish: ...Stay creaky.

ep2.title: Episode 2: Something in the Walls Is Singing
lines: *Theme music: a creaky door, then a kazoo.*
Trish: Update, listeners. We interviewed the next-door neighbor, Mrs. Pruitt.
Bev: Lovely woman. Eighty-two. Nine cats. One crossbow.
Trish: She says someone's been singing inside the walls of number twelve. At night. Bon Jovi.
Bev: That's the catfish.
Trish: Catfish don't sing, Bev.
Bev: Not with THAT attitude.
Trish: Mrs. Pruitt describes the singer as 'very flat, but very confident.'
Bev: Classic catfish.
Trish: She also says her bathwater keeps going cold. 'Like someone's in it with me.'
Bev: Trish, that's either a catfish or a very forward plumber.
Trish: Next week we go to the library. On purpose. Stay creaky!

ep3.title: Episode 3: The Inspector
lines: *Theme music: a creaky door, then a kazoo.*
Trish: This week, an exclusive. City building inspector Dan has agreed to talk to us.
Dan: Happy to be here, ladies. Big fan. I listen while I inspect. It's very soothing.
Bev: Dan. 12 Heartbreak Lane. Haunted? Yes or no.
Dan: The only thing haunting that house is its water pressure.
Trish: Is it true you asked the new owner out for coffee?
Dan: To discuss PERMITS. ...And then my shoes filled up with water. Both of them. On a dry day.
Bev: That's the catfish, Dan.
Dan: Also, there's a big storm forecast for next weekend. Batten down the hatches.
Trish: Next week: the library. Stay creaky!

ep4.title: Episode 4: We Went to the Library
lines: *Theme music: a creaky door, then a kazoo. Then, unusually, silence.*
Bev: Listeners. We went to the library.
Trish: We touched MICROFICHE, Bev.
Bev: And Trish found it. The local paper, 1987.
Trish: 'Local aerobics instructor Luke Moretti, 34, died while attempting to repair a sink on a first date.'
Bev: On a first DATE.
Trish: His date, a Brenda, told police he'd said he was 'great with his hands.'
Bev: Oh, Trish. That's tragic.
Trish: It is tragic.
Bev: A man died trying to impress a woman with his DIY. That's every man I've ever dated, Trish.
Trish: Most of them lived, Bev.
Bev: ...So no catfish?
Trish: No catfish, Bev. Stay creaky.

ep5.title: Episode 5: Case Closed (Mostly)
lines: *Theme music: a creaky door, a kazoo and, this week, a celebratory gong.*
Trish: We're LIVE from the front porch of 12 Heartbreak Lane. Case closed.
Bev: Mostly closed. I still think there's a catfish.
Trish: The new owner fixed every leak in the house. It passed inspection.
Bev: We asked her about Luke Moretti. She said, and I quote, 'It's complicated.'
Trish: Which, frankly, is the most romantic thing anyone's ever said about plumbing.
Bev: Also Dan the inspector says his shoes have been dry for a whole week, and he's never been so sad.
Trish: Final thoughts, Bev?
Bev: Never trust a man who says he's great with his hands.
*SPLASH. A bucket of water tips off the porch railing and soaks Bev completely.*
Trish: ...Stay creaky, everybody.
